## ✨ Highlights

- 🏗️ **Clusters as code**: Terraform's `janus_cluster` makes a cluster of new machines on the Controller's hypervisors - each on a physical host of its own by default -, its member count and its auto-scaling changed in place, its machines destroyed with it ([Terraform](https://janus.sw-servers.net/docs/terraform.md#janus_cluster)).
- ⚖️ **A cluster's machines go where there is the most memory**: made, recycled or added by scaling, a new machine goes to the host with the most memory to give, never to one without room for it ([on new machines](https://janus.sw-servers.net/docs/guide/clusters.md#on-new-machines)).

## 🔗 Clusters

- **`janus_cluster` in the Terraform provider** ([#299](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/299)):
  - `name`, the `hypervisors` its machines may go to, `anti_affinity` (`required` by default, `preferred`, `off`), `members`, the `machine` each member is (size, release, extensions, HAProxy branch, kernel, image, DHCP interfaces, DNS, NTP) and `autoscaling` (`observe`, `on`, `off`, its bounds and thresholds).
  - **`members` changes in place**: a member more is a new machine like the newest, placed by the anti-affinity; a member less is the newest, drained, taken out and destroyed. With `autoscaling` `on` it is the count the cluster starts with - the Controller decides afterwards, `current_members` says what it has.
  - **`autoscaling` changes in place**; removed, auto-scaling is off.
  - `name`, `hypervisors`, `anti_affinity` and `machine` make a new cluster; moving one to a newer release member by member is a recycle on the Controller.
  - Destroying it ends the cluster, then destroys its machines - those auto-scaling made too.
  - Computed: `current_members`, `member_names`, `machine_ids`. No import: the machine specification isn't read back from the Controller.
- **Placement by memory** ([#300](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/300)): among the hosts the anti-affinity allows, the one with the most memory free goes first - what a host keeps free (a twentieth, 512 MiB at least) aside, and what the same request already put there counted -; the order of the hypervisors given only breaks ties.
  - A host without room for one more machine is never picked: with too little memory anywhere, the cluster is refused before anything is made, saying what each host has.
  - With anti-affinity `off`, machines no longer go round the hypervisors in turn: they go where the memory is.
  - A recycle tries the hosts other than the replaced member's first - its memory is freed only once it leaves; a member more is placed the same way.
- **The auto-scaling policy's durations are in seconds** in the API: `out_after_seconds`, `in_after_seconds`, `out_cooldown_seconds`, `in_cooldown_seconds` - like a machine's policy - where v2026.10.24-6 gave nanoseconds ([#299](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/299)).
- The cluster's journal names a new machine's hypervisor ("on kvm02") where it gave the record's id ([#297](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/297)).

## 📖 Docs

- [Terraform](https://janus.sw-servers.net/docs/terraform.md#janus_cluster): `janus_cluster`; [clusters](https://janus.sw-servers.net/docs/guide/clusters.md#on-new-machines): where the machines go.
- [v2026.10.24-6's lab campaign](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/blob/main/docs/pre-release-tests/v2026.10.24-6.md), the first on two physical hosts: anti-affinity required refused before anything was made when the hosts were too few, two machines placed one on each host, a member recycled onto the only host left free, and a cluster scaled 2 → 3 → 2 under load with nothing lost ([#298](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/298)).

## 🧪 Tests

- `terraform-provider-test`: a `janus_cluster` of two new machines on the libvirt container, scaled to three and back to two in place - the third's machine destroyed -, its auto-scaling set, a plan with nothing left after each step, and destroyed with its machines.
- `controller-libvirt-test` checks the journal names the hypervisor on a recycle and a scale-out; the placement's unit tests cover memory in every anti-affinity mode.

## ⚠️ Upgrade notes

- **Auto-scaling policy fields**: `GET /api/clusters/{id}` and `PUT /api/clusters/{id}/autoscale` now use `*_seconds`. The nanosecond fields v2026.10.24-5 and -6 used (`out_after`, `in_after`, `out_cooldown`, `in_cooldown`) are still read - a policy saved by v2026.10.24-6 keeps its values -, but a script reading them should move to the new names.
- **`janus_cluster` needs a Controller on this version**: an older one doesn't read the policy in seconds.
- **Where machines go**: a cluster on hypervisors whose order you relied on - the first hypervisor first - is now placed by memory; the order only breaks ties.
